solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I am taking step towards this kind of painting

parts.note: contracted to I'm
pas is the French word for a dance step, used in English for ballet steps
to means towards, as in 'walk to the door'

explanation.surface: Someone says they are moving step by step towards a particular style of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the technique of laying paint on thickly so brush or knife marks stand out.

clue.text: Violently menaces a rich patron

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters being thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A wealthy benefactor turns nasty and threatens people.
explanation.definitionFit: Maecenas was a wealthy Roman who backed Virgil and Horace, and his name became a byword for a generous sponsor of the arts.

clue.text: River dweller, a mother's given up drink

parts.note: mother gives MA; the 's stands for 'has', joining it to what follows

indicators.note: in a down clue, given up means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: an otter lives by rivers

explanation.surface: A mother gives up her drink, along with an otter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' looks like abstaining, but in a down clue it means written upwards; the reversed animal still joins the charade last.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an almond-flavoured Italian liqueur, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Trip to cite part of Bible in competition

parts.note: a tour is a trip
to name someone is to cite them
NT is the New Testament, one part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A trip to quote scripture in some sort of contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a series of contests, a sporting competition.

clue.text: Regularly arraigned for violence

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: Someone is routinely brought before the court for violent offences.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage is violent anger or fury, so the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Greeting little Sarah before one in the morning

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah
a means one, as in 'a dog'
a.m. stands for the morning hours

explanation.surface: Saying hello to young Sarah ahead of one o'clock in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaam is a low bow with the hand to the forehead, a respectful Eastern salutation.

clue.text: See after last broadcast in an old-fashioned manner

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters before the cathedral city that follows
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of last are rearranged

parts.note: Ely is a see, a bishop's diocese in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Instructions to watch something after the final transmission, delivered in a dated way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the definition-looking verb but it is the diocese of Ely; 'broadcast' turns LAST into STAL, which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Done stalely means done in a stale, worn-out or outdated way.

clue.text: A close friend marks word with initials

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or pal
M abbreviates mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A good friend scores a word made of initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An acronym is a word formed from the first letters of other words, such as NATO.

clue.text: When in sea, it's rocky

indicators.note: in places the word for when inside the sea's name

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea in northern Europe
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Out at sea, the waters become rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' looks like rough water but it is the definition: made of basalt rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Basaltic describes something made of basalt, a dark volcanic stone, so it is rock-related.

clue.text: In afterthought bring back practice for group of stars

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the afterthought abbreviation

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

indicators.note: bring back means reverse the letters of the word for practice

parts.note: usage is customary practice

explanation.surface: Someone adds a note at the end of a letter urging a return to old habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus is a constellation of the northern sky, named after the winged horse.

clue.text: Liar goes around women's quarters

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A liar wanders about the women's part of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the harem, the part of a Muslim palace where wives and concubines lived.

clue.text: Inflammation sister has in situ painfully

indicators.note: has means holds, so the word for sister contains the rearranged letters
painfully suggests the letters being twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A nurse has local inflammation right where it hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' works as a container: the sibling holds the jumbled Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinusitis is a swelling of the sinus linings, a kind of inflammation.

clue.text: Part next to new waterway

parts.note: to part is to sever or separate

explanation.surface: A section beside a newly dug canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is the longest river in Britain, a natural waterway.

clue.text: Friend embraces British woman in opera in unusual manner

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the friend word wraps the other letters

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter
Norma is the title heroine of Bellini's opera

explanation.surface: A pal hugs a British opera singer in a strange way.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormally means in a way that departs from the usual, oddly.

clue.text: Fast cuckoo, one doing a marathon?

definitions.meaning: a speedy desert bird of the cuckoo family that runs rather than flies
whimsically, someone who runs a long race on the road

explanation.surface: A speedy madman runs a long race.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadrunner is an American cuckoo famed for speed on foot; whimsically, a marathon runner runs on roads.

clue.text: Model to remain fresh

definitions.meaning: a shoemaker's wooden foot-shaped form, a model on which shoes are shaped
to keep or endure without spoiling, as food that keeps well

explanation.surface: A model trying to stay young-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler's last is a model foot; food that lasts stays good, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Embroider surplus copies by gallery

parts.note: overs are extra copies printed beyond the order, a printing term
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Stitching decoration onto spare prints beside an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embroider' looks like needlework, but it means exaggerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider a story is to exaggerate it with invented detail.

clue.text: Such a journalist could be sistered

indicators.note: could be says these letters might become another word once rearranged

explanation.surface: A female journalist is supposedly the kind who could be made a sister.
explanation.definitionFit: An editress is a female editor, a dated term for a woman in journalism who runs a publication.

clue.text: Twice in this place, broadcast exclamation of approval

indicators.note: twice means the sounded word appears two times
broadcast means said on air, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: here means in this place

explanation.surface: Two cheers of agreement sent out on the airwaves from this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Called out in Parliament, the phrase signals agreement with a speaker.

clue.text: Sourness of detectives in island unknown

indicators.note: in puts the police abbreviation inside the small island word

parts.note: an ait is a small river island, as on the Thames
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Bitter detectives working on an island where nothing is known.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidity is sharpness of taste, the same as sourness.

clue.text: Measuring device encountered in more than half of America

indicators.note: in puts the word for encountered inside the shortened country name
more than half of keeps the first four of the seven letters

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: An instrument found in most of the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: Four of the country's seven letters count as more than half.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammeter is an instrument that measures electric current in amperes.

clue.text: Owed tenor for music

parts.note: money owed is due

explanation.surface: A singer owed payment in return for performing.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a piece of music for two performers.

clue.text: Device for reversing current short journey on a rocky height

indicators.note: short means losing the final letter of the word for a journey

parts.note: a commute is a daily journey to work
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A brief trip on a rocky peak, of a device that changes the flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A commutator in a motor or dynamo switches the direction of electric current.

clue.text: In Paris an archdeacon's odd

parts.note: une is the French for 'a' or 'an' with a feminine noun
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A strange French clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven numbers are odd ones, and uneven also means irregular or strange.

clue.text: Delivers more than one golf club without head

indicators.note: without head means dropping the first letter of the plural club

parts.note: putters are golf clubs used on the green

explanation.surface: Delivering a set of golf clubs with their heads missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without head' sounds like a broken golf club but it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter words is to deliver them, speak them out.

clue.text: Mark policeman getting series recast

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: recast means cast again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective who is given a new role in a TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: A dieresis is a diacritical mark of two dots over a vowel, as in naïve.

clue.text: International criminal is object of worship

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A global crook revered by followers.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a sacred image venerated in Orthodox churches, hence anything worshipped.

clue.text: Appropriates girl's former partners

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name; the 's is a link
exes are former spouses or lovers

explanation.surface: Someone helps themselves to a woman's old boyfriends.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex something is to seize it, to take it over as one's own.

clue.text: So without ultimate energy for it

indicators.note: without ultimate means dropping the last letter when it is the one named

parts.note: therefore means so
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Nothing left at the end, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' looks like a link but it is the starting word; 'for it' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal or archaic word meaning for that thing, in return for it.

clue.text: Time certain to produce destruction

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sure means certain

explanation.surface: An age bound to bring ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasure is rubbing out or wiping away, a form of obliteration.
